content.title: Lufthansa throws hat in ring in bidding for TAP stake
content.summary:
STORY: Germany's Lufthansa airline submitted a proposal on Thursday for a minority stake in Portugal's carrier TAP.

The company said it has formally filed its interest with the government via state holding company Parpublica.

Rivals British Airways and Air France-KLM have also expressed interest in buying up TAP's planned sale of shares.

Portugal's government relaunched a long-delayed privatization plan for TAP in July, putting a 44.9% stake up for sale to an airline that could add scale and competitiveness.

An additional 5% is to be sold to TAP employees.

The government said last month it expects the planned sale of the combined stake to proceed smoothly.

Airlines interested in TAP must formally submit a "manifestation of interest" by November 21 and non-binding offers in the coming months.

Lufthansa said its aspirations as an investor took into account TAP's, quote,  "great strategic importance to the European aviation industry."

content.title: Lufthansa Group Expresses Interest in Portugal’s TAP
content.summary: Lufthansa Group  formally expressed its interest in bidding for a stake in Portugal’s state-owned airline TAP Air Portugal.  The Portuguese government outlined its intention to sell a 49.9% stake in its national carrier in July, with 44.9% being reserved for private investors.  “TAP Air Portugal is of great strategic importance to the European aviation industry,” said  Carsten Spohr,  chairman and chief executive of Lufthansa Group.
